speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe when you first noticed this neck swelling and if it has changed in size since then? Also, have you experienced any pain, difficulty swallowing, or changes in your voice?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of colon cancer, have you experienced any unintentional weight loss, night sweats, or changes in your bowel habits recently? I will now palpate the mass to assess its consistency and mobility.

speaker: Doctor
text: On palpation, the mass is firm, non-tender, and fixed to the underlying tissues. I will now order a CT scan of the neck to evaluate the extent of the lesion and check for lymphadenopathy. REQUEST TEST: CT_Neck

speaker: Doctor
text: That is unexpected given the fixed nature of the mass; could you clarify if the swelling is specifically located in the midline or if it extends to the sides, and does it move when you stick out your tongue? REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Colon cancer (colectomy performed), type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, osteoarthritis of the left knee. Social history: Works as a traffic warden, frequently plays golf.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CT scan being normal despite a firm, fixed mass is puzzling, so I need to look closer at the tissue composition. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Overall healthy appearance, no other complaints or symptoms noted.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the location on the nape of the neck, the firm and fixed nature of the mass, and your history of diabetes, I suspect a deep neck space abscess or a complex cystic lesion that may not have been fully characterized by the initial CT. Let me examine the overlying skin for any signs of inflammation, dimpling, or a central punctum.
